subject: pharmacology
title: Pramipexole, MAO B and COMT Inhibitors, and Amantadine

steps.tx: **Pramipexole**, a non ergot D3 preferring dopamine agonist, serves Parkinson disease and restless legs syndrome at different dose altitudes, renally cleared and long acting enough for twice or thrice daily dosing. Its adverse signature defines agonist counselling: somnolence with sudden sleep attacks (driving warnings mandatory), peripheral oedema, hallucinations in older patients, and impulse control disorders that families often report before patients volunteer them.
steps.say: Pramipexole works smoothly and sedates suddenly; ask the family about sleep, ankles and impulses.

left.title: Pramipexole profile
points: Non ergot D2 D3 agonist, renal clearance
Parkinson adjunct and restless legs indications
Once daily extended release formulations exist
No ergot fibrosis burden

right.title: Counselling essentials
points: Sudden sleep episodes: driving and machinery warnings
Impulse control disorders screened with family input
Oedema and orthostatic symptoms reviewed
Taper on withdrawal: dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome

steps.tx: **Selegiline** irreversibly inhibits monoamine oxidase B at low oral doses, slowing striatal dopamine breakdown and modestly extending levodopa action, with selectivity lost as dose climbs toward MAO A and the tyramine cheese reaction territory. Its amphetamine metabolites can disturb sleep, so morning dosing rules. Transdermal selegiline in depression deliberately exploits higher exposure. In Parkinson practice it suits early mild disease and wearing off adjunct duty.
steps.say: Selegiline guards dopamine from MAO B; keep the dose selective, take it early, respect tyramine at the margins.

nodes.label: MAO B irreversibly inhibited in striatum
Dopamine breakdown slows, levodopa effect extends
Selectivity lost as dose rises toward MAO A
Tyramine pressor risk returns with lost selectivity

steps.tx: **Rasagiline**, the second generation MAO B inhibitor, is more potent, once daily, and free of amphetamine metabolites, with trials in early monotherapy and wearing off adjunct roles mirroring selegiline's map. Serotonin syndrome warnings with antidepressants and meperidine attach to the whole class by mechanism vigilance, though MAO B selectivity keeps absolute risk low at licensed doses. Ciprofloxacin and other CYP1A2 inhibitors raise rasagiline levels, its main metabolic flag.
steps.say: Rasagiline is selegiline refined: once daily, no amphetamine baggage, same serotonin vigilance.

left.title: Selegiline
points: Irreversible MAO B inhibition, twice daily oral
Amphetamine metabolites: insomnia if dosed late
Orally disintegrating and transdermal variants exist
Selectivity dose limited

right.title: Rasagiline
points: Once daily, more potent MAO B inhibition
No amphetamine metabolites
CYP1A2 inhibitors raise its levels
Early monotherapy and adjunct evidence

steps.tx: Catechol O methyltransferase (COMT) degrades levodopa peripherally to useless 3 O methyldopa; **entacapone** blocks COMT only outside the brain, taken with every levodopa dose to stretch its half life and smooth wearing off, tinting urine orange red harmlessly and adding dyskinesia and diarrhoea. Fixed triple tablets (levodopa carbidopa entacapone) package the choreography. Entacapone never works alone because it has no antiparkinsonian action without levodopa aboard.
steps.say: Entacapone rides with every levodopa dose, stretches it, and paints the urine orange for free.

nodes.label: Peripheral COMT blocked, 3 O methyldopa falls
Levodopa half life and on time extend
Levodopa dose often trimmed as dyskinesia appears

steps.tx: Peripherally, catechol O methyltransferase turns levodopa into inactive 3 O methyldopa. **Entacapone** inhibits the enzyme only outside the brain and is swallowed with every levodopa dose, which lengthens the half life and smooths wearing off. Urine becomes orange red, a harmless colour change. Extra dyskinesia and diarrhoea are the adverse effects that matter. Combination tablets of levodopa, carbidopa and entacapone simply fix the timing. Given without levodopa, entacapone has no antiparkinsonian effect at all.
steps.say: Entacapone blocks peripheral COMT so less of each levodopa dose is wasted as 3 O methyldopa. It is taken every time levodopa is taken, the effect lasts longer, and wearing off is smoother. Urine turns orange red without harm. Diarrhoea and more dyskinesia can occur. The drug does nothing unless levodopa is given with it.

vis.alt: A peripheral enzyme diagram shows COMT converting levodopa into 3 O methyldopa, with entacapone blocking that conversion.
vis.caption: Outside the brain, COMT is shown turning levodopa into inactive 3 O methyldopa until entacapone stops the enzyme. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Tolcapone** crosses into brain as well, inhibiting COMT centrally and peripherally with greater potency, and carries the class's dark history: fatal fulminant hepatitis in early use imposed strict liver enzyme surveillance schedules and reserve status behind entacapone failure. The contrast is a perfect examination dyad: same target, different barrier penetration, different monitoring universe. Any patient on tolcapone carries documented liver test cadence or should not be on it.
steps.say: Tolcapone is entacapone plus brain entry plus a liver monitoring contract; sign it or do not prescribe it.

left.title: Entacapone
points: Peripheral COMT inhibition only
With every levodopa dose
Orange urine, diarrhoea, dyskinesia increase
No liver monitoring programme required

right.title: Tolcapone
points: Central plus peripheral COMT inhibition
Thrice daily dosing, more potent smoothing
Fulminant hepatitis history: scheduled liver tests
Reserved after entacapone inadequacy

steps.tx: **Amantadine**, an old antiviral, weakly blocks NMDA glutamate receptors, promotes dopamine release and blocks its reuptake, a scatter of actions that uniquely suppresses levodopa induced dyskinesia while mildly helping parkinsonism itself, now formulated in extended release for that antidyskinetic niche. Its adverse set is equally distinctive: livedo reticularis (mottled legs), ankle oedema, confusion and hallucinations in the elderly, and withdrawal precipitating delirium or neuroleptic malignant like states if stopped abruptly.
steps.say: Amantadine is the dyskinesia damper with mottled legs; taper it, never drop it.

left.title: Amantadine actions
points: NMDA antagonism plus dopaminergic facilitation
Only oral drug with clear antidyskinetic effect
Mild antiparkinsonian benefit of its own
Extended release formulations for dyskinesia

right.title: Amantadine adverse set
points: Livedo reticularis and ankle oedema
Confusion and hallucinations in older patients
Renal clearance: dose by kidney function
Abrupt withdrawal risks delirium and rigidity crises

steps.tx: **Amantadine** began as an antiviral. In Parkinson disease it weakly blocks NMDA receptors, encourages dopamine release and slows dopamine reuptake. That mixture is unusual because it reduces levodopa dyskinesia and, more mildly, helps the parkinsonism itself. An extended release preparation is used for the dyskinesia indication. Mottled livedo reticularis on the legs and ankle oedema are characteristic, and older patients become confused or hallucinate. An abrupt stop can trigger delirium or an illness resembling neuroleptic malignant syndrome, so the dose is tapered.
steps.say: Amantadine weakly blocks NMDA receptors and alters dopamine release, which damps levodopa dyskinesia and gives mild help to the parkinsonism. Livedo on the legs and swollen ankles are typical, and older patients may grow confused. The drug is tapered rather than stopped suddenly, because an abrupt halt can cause delirium or a malignant syndrome like state.

vis.alt: Both lower legs show a persistent purple net like mottling of livedo reticularis during amantadine treatment.
vis.caption: The skin of both legs carries a lace like purple mottling, livedo reticularis, in someone taking amantadine. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Impulse control disorders** deserve a full step because they destroy households quietly: pathological gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive shopping and binge eating emerge in roughly one in six agonist treated patients, dose related, D3 mediated, and characteristically concealed by shame until debts announce them. Screening with direct, permission giving questions and family collateral, dose reduction or agonist withdrawal (tapering against withdrawal syndrome), and documentation protect patients better than any after the fact rescue.
steps.say: Ask about gambling, spending and sexuality directly; patients hide impulse disorders until the money is gone.

nodes.label: Impulse control disorder emerges, concealed by shame
Direct questions and family collateral surface it
Gradual agonist reduction with withdrawal vigilance

steps.tx: **Assemble wearing off therapy** as a ladder this module built: shorten levodopa intervals, add entacapone with each dose or an MAO B inhibitor once daily, add or adjust a dopamine agonist, deploy amantadine where dyskinesia caps levodopa, and refer for device aided therapies (apomorphine infusion, levodopa intestinal gel, deep brain stimulation) when oral choreography fails. Each rung is chosen against the patient's cognitive, psychiatric and autonomic reserve, not by algorithm alone.
steps.say: Fractionate, inhibit an enzyme, add an agonist, damp dyskinesia, then refer for devices; in that order, individualised.

left.title: Oral ladder rungs
points: Levodopa fractionation and protein timing
Entacapone per dose or MAO B inhibitor daily
Dopamine agonist added or optimised
Amantadine where dyskinesia limits levodopa

right.title: Device aided rung
points: Apomorphine intermittent rescue or infusion
Levodopa carbidopa intestinal gel infusion
Deep brain stimulation in suitable candidates
Criteria: refractory fluctuations despite oral optimisation
